Package sc.fiji.snt.gui

Class FileInspector

java.lang.Object
sc.fiji.snt.gui.FileInspector
public final class FileInspector extends Object
Classifies files and folders (e.g., those dropped onto a window) without ever blocking the caller for longer than a fixed budget. Intended to decide what to do with them before anything is imported.

Design rules:

  • All file system access happens on daemon worker threads. Blocking I/O (e.g., on a stalled network mount) cannot be interrupted, so probes that exceed their budget are abandoned, not canceled, and the result flags the item as FileInspector.Kind.UNREACHABLE
  • A circuit breaker skips further probes under a mount that recently timed out
  • Folders are classified from the names of a few sentinel files (session, Zarr and N5 datasets) without being listed. Other folders are listed shallowly, up to a fixed number of entries
  • Files are classified from their names. Only zip archives are sniffed: the central directory is read, but only its first entries are examined
  • Nothing is opened, parsed or imported
Author:
Tiago Ferreira

    • inspect

      public Future<?> inspect(File[] files, Consumer<FileInspector.Result> callback)
      Inspects the specified files in the background. Never blocks the caller, and never throws.
      Parameters:
      files - the files to be inspected
      callback - receives the result on the Event Dispatch Thread. It is always called exactly once, unless the returned future is canceled before the inspection completes
      Returns:
      a future that can be used to discard the result

    • inspectNow

      public FileInspector.Result inspectNow(File... files)
      Inspects the specified files, blocking for at most the total budget. Must not be called from the Event Dispatch Thread.
      Parameters:
      files - the files to be inspected
      Returns:
      the result. Never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called from the Event Dispatch Thread
